links.note: Was 32711 (Matching Lengths to Units). Measuring a comb, pen, pencil and eraser with a metre scale and noting the results is Activity 5.1, in 32704.
Was 32702 (Metre, Centimetre, Millimetre, Kilometre). The Column I / Column II matching of lengths to units is Table 5.5, the exercise described in 32711.
Was 32708 (The Passengers in Deepa's Bus), which is about reference points. Measuring cloth by a body length is the handspan/arm-length opening of 32699, where Deepa's mother's balisht appears.
Was 32701 (Why the World Agreed on SI). Why the five friends got different numbers for the same table is 32699's finding - their handspans differ.
Was 32700 (A Length Is a Number and a Unit). The metre as the SI unit of length is stated in 32701.
Was 32713 (The Thickness of One Page). Why the metre is inconvenient for very large distances is the closing question of 32702, with the railway track and the page thickness.
Was 32700 (A Length Is a Number and a Unit). That 1 mm is the smallest value a 15-cm scale can measure is stated in 32702.
Was 32711 (Matching Lengths to Units). Listing objects whose lengths are easier to express in mm, cm and m is the exercise in 32712.
Was 32707 (In Motion or at Rest). The rollercoaster item asks for all three kinds of motion on one track, which no single motion concept covers; 32712 is the exercise that sets it.

Was 32701 (Why the World Agreed on SI). Choosing which material Tasneem must not use for a metre scale is the exercise in 32712, and the reason - a scale must not change length - is stated nowhere else.
Was 32714 (A Bicycle That Measures Distance), a project. Expressing 1.5 km in metres needs the kilometre-to-metre relation stated in 32702.
Was 32700 (A Length Is a Number and a Unit). Measuring a curved base needs a thread or flexible tape, which is the instrument-choice content of 32703.
Was 32704 (Writing a Measurement Properly), which is the notation. Why standard units are worth agreeing on is 32701's argument.
Was 32700 (A Length Is a Number and a Unit). Placing the scale in contact along the object's length is the first of 32703's three points of technique.
Was 32700 (A Length Is a Number and a Unit). Using a scale with a broken zero by subtracting one full mark from the other is worked in 32703.
Was 32707 (In Motion or at Rest). The reference point is defined in 32705, through the garden-or-school disagreement.
Was 32708 (The Passengers in Deepa's Bus). The friends disagreeing over whether the garden is closer is 32705's own scene - each measured from their own house.
Was 32707 (In Motion or at Rest), which defines motion against rest. Linear motion is named in 32709.
Was 32707 (In Motion or at Rest). The merry-go-round is 32709's example of circular motion.
Was 32707 (In Motion or at Rest). A swing moving to and fro about a fixed position is oscillatory motion, defined in 32710.
Was 32711 (Matching Lengths to Units). The International System of Units is named in 32701.
